title: Fuselage — Main Deck Floor Frames 40 to 54 — Freighter Hard Point Provisioning
abstract: Retrofit of sixteen machined hard points and reinforced floor panel edges between frames 40 and 54, so that a later freighter conversion becomes a bolt-on rather than a rebuild of the floor grid.

sections.planning_reason: Conversion houses were removing and re-installing the entire main deck floor grid between frames 40 and 54 because the passenger build has no load introduction points where the freighter restraint system needs them. That work accounts for around 40 per cent of the conversion downtime and produces a fatigue-critical re-drilled joint that has to be substantiated aircraft by aircraft. Lessors with conversion candidates in the fleet asked for the provisions to be available as a retrofit so that the aircraft can be prepared during an ordinary check years before the conversion itself.
sections.description: Sixteen machined hard points are installed in the cargo floor panel structure between frames 40 and 54, four per bay, aligned with the freighter restraint grid. The aft floor gusset kit is replaced by a heavier item, the forward splice plate is extended outboard, and an upper lug is added at each hard point as the load introduction fitting. In passenger configuration the hard points are capped and carry no load.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Remove the cabin floor covering and the seats between frames 40 and 54. CAUTION: SUPPORT THE FLOOR PANELS BEFORE THE FASTENERS ARE REMOVED. Do AMM-S-53-50-13-000-006-A to remove the cargo floor panels in the affected bays. Remove the aft floor gusset kit D5350137657469 and the forward splice plate sub-assembly ES657922-93 in each bay. Install the heavier gusset kit and the extended splice plate, wet with sealant. Ream the hard point holes using the drill jig and do an eddy current inspection of each reamed hole. Install the upper lug sub-assemblies HA342629-96 at each of the sixteen positions and torque them to the value in the accomplishment instructions. Fit the caps to all sixteen hard points. Do AMM-S-53-50-13-400-006-A to install the cargo floor panels, using countersunk screws AGS895094-3D at the reduced pitch across the reinforced edges. Re-secure the seat track lock actuator position 8300VU. Install the seats and the floor covering. Do the floor loading check and record the embodiment and the revised empty mass.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to SOLANO-30 and SOLANO-34 aircraft from MSN S01046 up to the production cut-in at MSN S01705, and only to aircraft that already carry the chromate-free protection and drainage standard in the lower shell, because the hard point feet sit in the same drain path. Aircraft below MSN S01046 have a different floor beam standard and are outside the scope.
sections.material_note: Kit K5350-1045-01 contains the gusset kits, the splice plates, the sixteen lug assemblies, the caps and the fastener set. Lead time is twenty-six weeks. The mass increase of 63 kg is significant for a passenger operator and the Service Bulletin says plainly that the retrofit is normally only economic when a conversion is already planned.

type_data.compliance_time: At the operator's discretion, normally at a scheduled C-check before the aircraft is committed to a freighter conversion.
